title: IAM Roles for ECS and EC2
description: Remove access keys entirely by using IAM roles for EC2 instances and ECS tasks.

data.text: IAM roles provide temporary credentials to AWS resources. Instead of storing access keys in code or environment variables, your EC2 instances or ECS tasks assume a role and receive credentials automatically.

rows: Containerized apps on ECS or Fargate
Allows ECS to pull images and write logs

data.text: Create an IAM Role for ECS

data.title: Create a task role with AWS CLI
data.content: Create a role that allows reading secrets from Secrets Manager.
data.code:
# Create the role
aws iam create-role --role-name aspnet-ecs-task-role --assume-role-policy-document file://ecs-trust-policy.json

# Attach Secrets Manager policy
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name aspnet-ecs-task-role --policy-name ReadSecrets --policy-document file://secrets-manager-policy.json

data.text: When the app runs on EC2 or ECS with an assigned role, the AWS SDK automatically retrieves temporary credentials from the instance metadata service.

data.title: Same code works locally and in AWS
data.content: No access keys or secrets are required when using IAM roles.

data.title: Remove access keys from local settings
data.description: After configuring IAM roles, remove credentials from local environment variables.
steps: Create an IAM role with Secrets Manager access
Attach the role to the ECS task definition or EC2 instance
Deploy the app to ECS or run on EC2
Verify the app still reads secrets successfully
data.expectedOutcome: The app runs in AWS without any long-lived credentials in environment variables.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: IAM roles provide temporary credentials to AWS resources
The AWS SDK automatically uses instance metadata for credentials
Avoid long-lived access keys in code or environment variables
data.takeaway: IAM roles are the AWS-native replacement for access keys. Once configured, your C# code never touches a permanent secret.
